chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me; he said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyri narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, in his long hadith.
He said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

When the believer is resurrected from his grave, a likeness (image) of him comes out with him from his grave, walking ahead of him. Whenever the believer sees a terror from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection, the likeness says to him, 'Do not grieve and do not be alarmed, and give glad tidings of joy and honor from Allah.' It will not cease giving him glad tidings of joy and honor from Allah until he stands before Allah, Exalted is His Glory. He will be given a slight accounting, and he will be ordered to Paradise, with the likeness ahead of him. The believer will say to him, 'May Allah have mercy on you, you were a good companion with me from my grave, and you did not cease giving me glad tidings of joy and honor until I saw that. Who are you?' It will say, 'I am the joy that you gave to your believing brother. Allah created me from it to give you glad tidings.'

key_terms.أَهْوَالُ یَوْمِ الْقِیَامَهِ: Terrors of the Day of Resurrection

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'likeness' that accompanies a believer from the grave on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical reality of *surr* (joy/pleasure) as a tangible entity that accompanies the believer from the grave, serving as a divine comforter during the awe-inspiring events of the Day of Judgment. This hadith provides a profound Shia theological insight into the concept of *thawab* (reward), illustrating how the spiritual act of making a brother happy manifests as a literal companion that testifies to the believer’s character and facilitates an easy reckoning. The narrative underscores the interconnectivity of the community of believers, where one’s emotional generosity becomes an eternal asset in the hereafter.
